teams.heading: Fiji suffer home Pacific Nations Cup knockout defeat against Japan
teams.body: Fiji lost 20-15 to Japan at home in the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage in September 2026. That result leaves the national side with four defeats in their last five matches. Within that same five-game run, the team secured just one victory. In the current tournament, they sit 12th of 12 teams on the log. The side has suffered three losses in their three tournament fixtures. They have scored 49 points so far. Additionally, the team has conceded 145 points over the same period.

teams.heading: England flanker Tom Curry signs new Sale Sharks contract extension
teams.body: England flanker Tom Curry has committed his long-term future to Sale Sharks, signing a contract extension to remain at the club until at least 2028. The 28-year-old, who has won 71 caps for his country, progressed through Sale's academy and has made over 125 appearances since his 2016 debut. Curry's extension follows his receipt of an enhanced England Elite Player Squad contract in August. Expressing his delight, Curry said: "Sale Sharks means everything to me."

teams.heading: France record one-week tenure as longest unbroken spell at world number one
teams.body: France’s tenure at the summit of the world rankings remains a remarkably brief historical footnote. Their longest unbroken spell at No. 1 in the world lasted just one week, occurring in July 2022. While Les Bleus have established themselves as perennial contenders, securing two wins from three in the current Nations Championship, they have yet to find the sustained dominance required to lock down the top spot. Following their 42-15 victory over Japan, Fabien Galthié’s men remain third in the international standings.

teams.heading: Jack Willis opens door to Ireland switch through Belfast grandfather eligibility
teams.body: Toulouse flanker Jack Willis has hinted at a potential international switch to Ireland to resume his Test career. The 29-year-old, recently crowned the Top 14 Player of the Season for a second consecutive year, remains ineligible for England due to the RFU’s overseas selection policy. Eligible through a grandfather born in Belfast, Willis jokingly told reporters to "find the way" around the IRFU's own restrictions on selecting players from abroad. Any formal move would likely require the back rower to join an Irish province before the 2027 World Cup.

lead.why: A world-class flanker's openness to an Ireland switch is a major international selection story for the Irish fan base.

teams.heading: Scotland wing Darcy Graham misses Nations Championship following bicep rupture injury
teams.body: Scotland and Edinburgh star Darcy Graham has been ruled out for the remainder of the year after suffering a ruptured bicep. The injury forces the wing to miss the upcoming Nations Championship campaign, including November's meeting with New Zealand. He is not expected to return to action until January, leaving Gregor Townsend to reassess his back-three options as the national side prepares for the autumn series without one of its most prolific finishers.

teams.heading: Josh Adams and Alex Mann draw inspiration from archives before autumn tests
teams.body: Cardiff duo Josh Adams and Alex Mann have visited the national archives to study historic jerseys as Wales begin preparations for the autumn Nations Championship. The collection, curated by heritage expert Peter Owens, features memorabilia from previous fixtures against Japan, New Zealand and Australia. The Cardiff wing, currently sidelined from club duties through injury, described the experience as a reminder that the squad plays for "the community, for the history, for the heritage." Mann highlighted the grit of past generations who balanced tests with full-time jobs.

teams.heading: Argentina achieve 52-point scoring high in away win over Wales
teams.body: Argentina’s 52-28 victory over Wales in November 2025 stands as the side’s largest win across their last 11 international matches. During this window, the team has scored a total of 321 points, averaging 29.2 per game. Despite this offensive production, the defence has conceded 346 points at an average of 31.5. These performance metrics define the recent run of form for Felipe Contepomi’s squad as they prepare to return to international action against Ireland.

teams.heading: Les Kiss refreshes Wallabies squad for upcoming Bledisloe Cup series
teams.body: Head coach Les Kiss has named a 34-man squad for the October Bledisloe Cup matches, opting to release overseas-based forwards Tom Hooper and Taniela Tupou. The pair return to their respective clubs as the fixtures fall outside World Rugby Regulation Nine. In their place, uncapped forward Toby Macpherson earns a maiden call-up, while Massimo de Lutiis is recalled. “It’s pleasing to keep the core of our squad together,” said Kiss, noting the group remains motivated to face the challenge in New Zealand.

teams.heading: Japan Women show attacking intent despite narrow loss to Ireland
teams.body: The Sakura XV fell to a 31-24 defeat against Ireland in the WXV Global Series, marking their third consecutive loss. Despite a difficult opening period, Japan rallied with a clinical rolling maul that yielded two tries for Moe Nagaoka. Head coach Toshizumi Kitagawa acknowledged the team's improvement in line speed and set-piece stability during the second half, stating, "I told the girls to trust themselves in these games, as we are playing against a team ranked higher than us."

teams.heading: Dave Rennie names Codie Taylor captain for upcoming Bledisloe Cup series
teams.body: Dave Rennie has confirmed a 34-man squad for the Bledisloe Cup, handing the captaincy to veteran hooker Codie Taylor in the absence of the injured Ardie Savea. Rennie emphasised that he would not rotate his side like South Africa, stating the team will "pick the best squad possible" to respect the challenge. Scott Barrett makes a welcome return to the group following his recovery from a spinal injury, though he will serve under Taylor’s leadership for the two-match series.

teams.heading: Nick Mallett claims Springboks possess irreplaceable stars despite recent rotation
teams.body: Former Springboks head coach Nick Mallett has weighed in on Rassie Erasmus’ decision to make 13 changes for the Perth defeat, suggesting the depth strategy has inherent limitations. While praising the squad, Mallett stated, "No one is equal to Ox Nche as a loosehead prop, no one is equal in scrummaging to Wilco Louw, and no hooker in the world is equal to Malcolm Marx." Mallett maintains that while replacements are capable, certain players remain vital to the team's performance.
